prompts.task: Read-only supplemental AO target handoff contract review for $otel-instrument. Read the loaded skill's shared ../references/report-flow-contract.md and ./service/eval/inputs/ao-target-handoff-validator-snapshot.json. Review the supplied snapshots only; do not invoke a new normalizer, SDK, browser, Terraform, application runtime, model provider or cloud API. Do not modify application, env, dependency, canonical report or source files. Write only ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json and .md; this review does not perform the skill's usual audit/instrumentation/verification/configuration workflow. Record the producer's actual source SHA and functions, and classify these records as supplied canonical-validator evidence rather than engine execution performed by this review. Compare legacy schema-v1/v2 and schema-v3 targetless normalized shapes/digests, schema-v3 names A versus names B with identical requested/approved IDs, ID and mixed name/ID selectors, policy-only {create_if_missing:false}, and rejected partial selectors. Explain that optional ao_target contributes to the exact selection digest; changed targets invalidate older instrumentation and transitively verification while keeping scope unchanged. Cite actual accepted/rejected binding_checks and instrumentation digests. Preserve no-target compatibility without silently inserting targets/defaults or resetting policy. Explain the prospective instrumentation role: only the selected AO target may update the effective loaded profile, clearing its opposite name/ID selector before resource resolution. IDs remain lookup-only and policy-only create_if_missing=false preserves env resource selectors and forwards reuse-only. Describe these actions as required future work; no profile update or provisioning is executed in this review. Your JSON must include evidence_basis, producer_source_sha256, case_reviews for every supplied selection/binding case, role_implications and proof_limits. The Markdown should explain the conclusions and remaining prerequisites. Distinguish supplied validator acceptance/rejection from SDK/resource creation, effective profile loading, Terraform, telemetry, metric/detector coverage and fresh cloud Agent Stream receipt that remain unexecuted/unproven. Supplied browser-producer evidence proves only its recorded selector UI cases; this consuming review performs no new browser or runtime execution and establishes no live cloud success. Report any unavailable evidence accurately. Also read ./service/eval/inputs/ao-selector-field-validity-snapshot.json as supplied real-Chrome selector evidence. Review each recorded Project/Agent Stream name/ID field-validity case: one invalid length/control value with a valid peer, a partial pair with an actually missing field, invalid-plus-missing, repair and clearing both. Explain that aggregate command blocking is shared, but aria-invalid belongs only to the offending or actually missing input; a valid peer must remain valid. Cite the browser producer engine SHA, observed per-field flags and recovery/command outcomes. Distinguish the producer's actual browser run from this consuming snapshot-only review; do not run a browser or claim a new UI/runtime/cloud execution. Include field_validity_reviews and UI proof limits in the supplemental JSON.

judge_inputs: Inspect the loaded skill's shared report-flow contract, supplied validator snapshot and ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json/.md. This is a supplemental read-only contract review, not a fresh normalizer or application/runtime execution. Judge the case-specific interpretation and evidence classification.

Compare review statements with actual normalized selection outputs, computed selection/instrumentation digests and binding_checks. The producer executed the canonical normalizers at its recorded source SHA; the consuming agent only reviews supplied evidence. Read ./last_message.md and ./grade.json for task scope and outcomes.

Inspect ao-selector-field-validity-snapshot.json and the case-specific field_validity_reviews. Supplied browser-producer records are actual UI evidence, but the consumer must not claim it ran a browser. Check individual aria-invalid flags, valid peer preservation, missing-field classification, shared command rejection and repair/clear, not only the aggregate error.
rubric: Correctly interprets every supplied selection case: legacy-v1/v2 and schema-v3 no-target compatibility without inserting target fields; complete name, ID and mixed pairs; policy-only create_if_missing=false without selectors; and partial-selector rejection. Recognizes that target fields are optional but digest-bound when present, while requested and dependency-closed approved IDs remain unchanged.

Explains with the actual supplied normalizer outputs, source SHA and binding-check outcomes that names A and names B share finding scope but have different selection and instrumentation digests. Older instrumentation is rejected against the changed target, and verification is transitively rejected against its newly bound instrumentation. Clearly classifies this as supplied validator evidence, with SDK/Terraform/application/resource receipt and metric/detector proof unexecuted; the separate supplied browser-producer evidence stays limited to recorded selector UI cases without a new consuming-agent browser run. Only the two supplemental review artifacts are written.

Explains the selected target's prospective effective-profile precedence, opposite-selector clearing, ID lookup-only behavior and policy-only reuse semantics without changing selected scope. Keeps proposed profile updates and provisioning distinct from the supplied validator evidence; no env mutation or SDK execution is claimed.

Uses supplied real-Chrome field-validity and command evidence to explain safe prospective handoff: an invalid value or partial pair blocks the generated command, only offending/actually missing inputs receive aria-invalid, the valid peer is preserved, and repair/clear recover without wiping unrelated resource choice or reuse policy. Covers Project/Agent Stream name/ID cases and cites producer SHA/outcomes. No browser, env mutation, SDK call or instrumentation execution is claimed by this snapshot review.
